title.narrative: Transport Network Development Investment Program - Tranche 2

description.narrative:
Tranche 2 will finance outputs under both components of the approved MFF:
Component A: Transport Infrastructure Development a) reconstruction and widening of the approximately 106 kilometer (km) Sapary to Jalalabad Road (the second section of the Kabul to Jalalabad Road), including provision of related design and construction supervision services; b) rehabilitation of the approximately 32 km Chan-e-Anjir to Gereshk Road, (the second section of the Lashkar Gah to Gereshk Road), including provision of related design and construction supervision services; and c) reconstruction of the approximately 50 km Sharan to Angoor Ada Road in Paktika, including provision of related design and construction supervision services.
All road infrastructure development projects under Tranche 2 have been designed to include community development and security plans.
Component B: Transport Network Management Capacity Development a) capacity building for the Ministry of Public Works (MPW) including restructuring support based on a revised business plan and design and implementation of an asset management system; and b) provision of support for project management and investment program implementation to MPW including procurement oversight, construction and contract supervision, safeguard policy and plan preparation and implementation, and feasibility studies to prepare subsequent tranches of the investment program.
Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: 115 km [Sapary-Jalalabad (33km), Sharan-Angoor Ada (50km), and Chan-e-Anjir-Gereshk (32km) sections) of reconstructed, rehabilitated, and appropriately maintained national and regional highways. Indicator: By 2020: The international roughness index of project roads less than 5 meters per km, compared with a current estimate of greater than 7 meters per km Achievement: 5 Progress/Status: 1. Sapary - Jalalabad road contract awarded to Xinjiang Beixin Road and Bridge Group Co. Ltd. (PRC) on 4 Dec. 2013. The contractor mobilized in Feb. 2014. Due to inaccessibility of contractor to worksite, the contractor and MPW agreed to reduced the scope of contract from 106 km to 33 km on 2 April 2018. The reduced scope completed in Dec. 2019.
2. Sharan - Angor Ada road contract awarded to the JV of MAB Construction Company Ltd. and Hamid Kandahari Construction Co. The contractor mobilized on 18 April 2015. The civil works for 50 km completed in 2019.
3. Chah-e-Anjir- Greshk Road awarded to Rauf Aziz Construction and Supply Co. The contract signed on 4 Oct. 2015. The contractor, consultant, and PMO project team have been able to work together well, resulting in satisfactory implementation progress despite the difficulties due to security threats in the project area. The civil works for 32 km completed in Feb. 2020.
Data Source: MPW progress reports

Rehabilitated and reconstructed sections of national and regional highways.

By 2020: Reduced travel time from Lashkar Gah to Gereshk from 4 hours to 2 hours Achievement: 2 Progress/Status: The contract of Chah-e-Anjir to Gereshk road subproject awarded in Oct. 2015 and contractor mobilized in Feb. 2016. Due to security reasons and military operations in the project area; the physical works have been suspended from June until end of Oct. 2018. The road completed in end Feb. 2020. As of 31 July 2021, the list of remaining 2 APs are under MoF process, and the compliance report is prepared and will be finalized once the remained 2 affected person receive their compensation.
Due to the suspension of AFG operations since the fall of the former government on 14 August 2021, the EA's compliance with reporting requirements for safeguards remains subject to a resumption of ADB operations on Afghanistan. Data Source: Socioeconomic surveys

By 2020: Reduced travel time from Jalalabad to Kabul from 5 hours to 4 hours. Achievement: 4 Progress/Status: The civil works contract of Sapary - Jalalabad package awarded and mobilized in Feb. 2014. However, in Oct. 2017 contractor suspended all works due to inaccessibility to work site. The government and contractor agreed to de-scope the contract in April 2018. The total length decreased to 33 km from 106km. The major change in scope was approved by the President on 9 Aug. 2019. The 33Km road of Sapary-Surkhrod completed on 31 Dec. 2019. Data Source: Traffic counts and surveys

By 2020: Reduced travel time along the Paktika Economic Corridor, from border of Pakistan to provincial capital of Sharan, from 7 hours to 3 hours. Achievement: 3 Progress/Status: The two roads sections (Section 1 - 23km of Sarhowza to Urgon Road and Section 2 for 24.7 km of Toray Tangay to Shakin Border Crossing Point) completed in January 2018 and September 2019, respectively. The project completion report has been received. Traffic counts are yet to be conducted.
Due to the suspension of AFG operations since the fall of the former government on 14 August 2021, the EA's compliance with reporting requirements for safeguards remains subject to a resumption of ADB operations on Afghanistan. Data Source: MPW and MOTCA records
